validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed at high tier, independent of GEM/gem.wiki. FERC Federal Register notice (Docket No. CP20-155-000, filed by Dakota Natural Gas, LLC (DNG), 1900 Cardinal Lane, Faribault, MN, seeking an NGA sec. 7(f) service-area determination in Traill County, ND) states DNG 'intends to construct approximately 62.74 miles of new pipeline in Minnesota and North Dakota' -- matches GEM's LengthKnown=63 mi almost exactly. Independently, Forum News Service/Ann Bailey (via inforum.com, Sep 29 2020), Hillsboro Banner (Cole Short, Mar 19 2021), Grow Hillsboro ND / Hillsboro Banner reprint (Feb 25 2020), Mayville-Portland Chamber site (mayvilleportland.com), and Prairie Public (public radio, Dec 5 2023) all independently describe the same physical project: a lateral built by Dakota Natural Gas connecting to the Viking Gas Transmission interstate pipeline (P0278, already tracked separately) in western Minnesota, crossing the Red River near Nielsville, MN, running south on Highway 200 to Hillsboro then west to Mayville, ND. The Prairie Public piece (2023, most recent) confirms Hillsboro and Mayville service was 'expanded 2021' and the company was still actively building out (Portland extended 2022; Larimore/Arvilla next), i.e. this system is a real, currently-operating asset, not a GEM-only entity. Route/owner/fuel-source are solid; see the concern objects below for what needs correcting. Opened 6 of the row's 3 harvested wiki citations directly (EIA aggregate portal, Inforum, Hillsboro Banner) plus 4 more found via open search (FERC Federal Register notice, growhillsborond.com, mayvilleportland.com, Prairie Public) -- all read to exhaustion for every column.

validity.recommendation: Flag PipelineType for review -- consider tagging as a distribution lateral (or at minimum noting the distinction in ResearcherNotes), same open question already raised in this batch for P0306 Doosan Bobcat / P0329 Tungsten to Bobtail.
validity.researcher_notes: PipelineType is blank on the sheet. Every independent source describes this as a small local DISTRIBUTION system, not an interstate transmission line: 4-inch steel main plus 6-inch high-density-plastic distribution pipe in town (Hillsboro Banner), built and operated by a company its own CEO calls 'the gas distributor' (Grow Hillsboro ND / Hillsboro Banner, Feb 25 2020 quote from Greg Palmer), delivering gas FROM the Viking Gas Transmission interstate trunk (P0278) directly TO ~750 residential/commercial end-use customers (American Crystal Sugar, Mayville State University, Traill County, city governments) rather than to another transmission system or bulk offtaker. The FERC docket itself frames this as a distribution service-area determination under NGA sec. 7(f) (not a sec. 7(c) certificate for interstate transmission capacity), and notes the pipeline is otherwise subject to STATE utility-commission jurisdiction (ND PSC approved it Sept 23, 2020) -- the normal posture for a distribution system, not a FERC-certificated transmission line. This doesn't make the row a phantom or a duplicate -- the asset is real and well documented -- but GGIT is nominally a transmission tracker and this project's own participants describe it as distribution. Recommend a human classification call rather than a unilateral fix.

validity.researcher_notes: Delayed=yes / DelayType=inferred looks like an automatic staleness inference (LastUpdated=2023-08-08, >1yr with no refs) rather than a documented fact. Every source says the opposite: Hillsboro Banner (Mar 2021) reports construction 'a month ahead of schedule' ('we are way ahead of schedule because of the mild winter' -- Dakota Natural Gas senior technician); the original target dates (August 2021 Hillsboro, late September 2021 Mayville, per Inforum Sep 2020) were met; and Prairie Public (Dec 2023) describes Hillsboro/Mayville as already 'expanded 2021' with the company having since moved on to Portland (2022) and a new Larimore-Arvilla project, i.e. business-as-usual continued buildout, not a stalled/delayed project. I found no source describing any slippage, missed milestone, or dormancy on this specific line. Recommend clearing rather than leaving an unsupported 'yes'.

validity.researcher_notes: Two independent sources agree on $8.5 million and neither supports $9,000,000: Forum News Service/Ann Bailey via inforum.com (Sep 29 2020) -- 'Construction on an $8.5 million pipeline project will begin in October in Traill County' -- and Hillsboro Banner/Cole Short (Mar 19 2021, a genuinely separate outlet/byline from the Forum News wire) -- 'Construction of an $8.5 million natural gas pipeline headed for homes in Hillsboro and Mayville is a month ahead of schedule.' Note the EARLIER estimate at the Feb 25, 2020 board-vote stage was $10-15 million (Grow Hillsboro ND / Hillsboro Banner reprint) -- the project came in under that initial estimate, and $8.5M is the figure both contemporaneous construction-era reports use. validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's single Diameter=4in only captures part of the system. Inforum (Sep 2020) independently corroborates the material split without the exact second number: 'The pipeline will be made of steel except in Hillsboro and Mayville, where it will be high-density plastic.' Recording only '4' silently drops the 6-inch in-town distribution main -- the same multi-diameter-on-one-row pattern this batch already handles elsewhere with comma-separated values (e.g. P0207 Kern River '36, 42').
